title: Frayed edge mini-audit: quick quality heuristics
content:
Purpose:
Quick, small-batch audit for weird output modes surfaced in nightly sampling (2/10 run). Not a formal eval — sketchpad for hypotheses and triage steps. Keep it short so I actually finish this.

Context/why: 
- After the 2/10 rollout we started seeing more truncated lists and occasional factual drift on product-summary prompts.
- Ops reported a small spike in token-timeouts around 02:00 UTC coincident with a heavy scheduling event (dedicated pool bump).

Quick hypothesis: 
1) batching/autobatching changes + new kernel selection -> different attention rounding -> more early-stopping in long enumerations.
2) fallback model routing (to a quantized variant) triggered for some SLOs -> subtle style/content shift.
3) prompt truncation at request layer when metadata grows (edge case) -> partial outputs.

Ad-hoc rubric (for ~20 sample pairs, small-batch):
- Pass/Fail semantics (fast): 0/1
- Fidelity: does the output include all requested items? (full/partial/missing) -> map to 0/0.5/1
- Hallucination: clear invented facts? (none/minor/major) -> 0/1/2
- Style drift: matched baseline tone? (yes/no) -> 0/1
- Latency artifact: did the output abruptly stop or append ellipses? (none/soft/hard) -> 0/0.5/1
Notes: combine into quick score (lower better).

Sample prompts used (trimmed):
1) "Summarize product X for enterprise buyers in 3 bullet points, include security and pricing caveat."
2) "List the 5 common failure modes of LLM inference runtimes with a one-sentence mitigation for each."
3) "Expand this micro-release note into a customer-facing blurb (2 short paragraphs); keep concise."

Representative outputs (baseline vs current) — lightly redacted: 
- Prompt 2 
Baseline (previous model):
"1) Tokenization mismatch — standardize inputs; 2) KV cache eviction — use larger cache; 3) Batching overload — tune batch size; 4) Hardware preemption — pin critical tasks; 5) Model regression — have rollback plan."

Current (observed):
"1) Tokenization mismatch — standardized inputs; 2) KV cache eviction — increase cache; 3) Batching overload — monitor batch size; 4) Hardware preemption — ???
"
Observations: missing a mitigation sentence for #4, #5 dropped entirely. Also phrasing changed from directive to passive tone. Got truncated abruptly (hard latency artifact).

- Prompt 1 
Baseline: three crisp bullets mentioning security (data isolation), compliance (audit logs), pricing (usage tiers).
Current: two bullets, second one conflates pricing and compliance, mentions a non-existent feature 'auto-protect' (hallucination minor).

Quick scoring summary (sample of 8 checked):
- 3/8 mostly okay (score <1.0)
- 4/8 partial/missing items (score 1.0-2.5)
- 1/8 clear hallucination + truncation (score >2.5)

Immediate triage steps (do now):
- Re-run the 02:00 UTC mini-batch with explicit routing to non-quantized variant (control). Compare token counts, truncation points. (Owner: Kiara)
- Pull scheduler logs around 01:55-02:05 and cross-check for preemption events. (Owner: SRE: Meera)
- Flip a feature-flag to disable new kernel selection heuristics for a rolling 1hr window and sample. (Owner: Runtime Eng)

Longer-term probing (ideas):
- Add a short synthetic test that asks for 5 enumerated items and asserts count/terminator tokens; run as part of nightly smoke.
- Add metadata-length guarding in the request layer with a hard cap + explicit truncation indicator in response headers; see if partial outputs correlate.
- Instrument fallback routing reasons to include explicit tag in response (e.g., routed_via=quantized-xx).

Notes to self / scratch: 
- When generating samples, preserve seed and full request metadata (user_id anonymized) so we can repro.
- Check PR 1242 for kernel heuristics diff (probably the simplest change that could explain style shift).
- Isolated failure seems to cluster on requests with long metadata blobs (internal note). Need to validate.

Open questions: 
- How often did fallback to quantized variants actually happen post-rollout? (ask runtime team)
- Can we correlate truncation points with batch sizes? (requires sampling instrumentation)
- Are any customers hitting this in production or only internal QA? (ask CS)

To-do (short):
- [ ] Run controlled rerun (today) with non-quantized routing.
- [ ] Export 50 pairs (baseline/current) into a tiny sheet for annotators.
- [ ] Post a short note to #model-quality with examples and tag product/CS for impact assessment.

Quick links (for me):
- INF ticket -> https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-789
- Kernel PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1242
- Slack thread id -> slack:#model-quality (thread pinned 02/11)

Final quick thought: start with simplest repro (1 prompt that asks for 5 items) and toggle routing and kernel heuristics one axis at a time. Keep dataset tiny and deterministic. If truncation persists even on non-quantized models, look hard at request-layer truncation or streaming cutoffs.

-- Kiara
